title: Execution plan reading workflow
description: Develop a repeatable workflow for reading, interpreting, and troubleshooting SQL Server execution plans.

data.text: An execution plan is SQL Server's recipe for fulfilling a query. Reading it fluently turns abstract performance complaints into concrete, fixable problems. The best workflow starts with the big picture and drills into the expensive operators one by one.

data.title: Two kinds of execution plans
items: Estimated plan: generated before execution using current statistics; useful for quick checks
Actual plan: generated after execution; includes actual row counts, warnings, and runtime metrics

data.text: Always compare estimated rows to actual rows. A large gap indicates stale statistics or a parameter-sensitive plan. The actual plan also shows warnings such as implicit conversions, missing indexes, and spills to tempdb.

data.title: Step-by-step workflow
items: Check the overall cost and identify the top three most expensive operators
Look for warnings: implicit conversions, missing index suggestions, spills, or timeouts
Verify that index seeks are used where expected and scans are justified by row counts
Trace the data flow from left to right, noting row count changes at each operator
Examine join types and join order for large row count mismatches
Confirm that the final output matches the query requirements without unnecessary columns

data.title: Capture an actual execution plan
data.content: Enable the execution plan in SSMS or set the XML option to capture plans programmatically.

data.title: Use the properties window
data.text: Click any operator in SSMS and press F4 to see its properties. Look for Estimated Number of Rows, Actual Number of Rows, Number of Executions, and Warnings. These properties tell you whether the optimizer's guess was accurate.

data.title: Symptoms that usually need investigation
items: Clustered index scan on a large table with a highly selective predicate
Key lookup with a high row count
Hash match with a spill warning to tempdb
Nested loops with millions of executions on the inner side
Implicit conversion on an indexed column in a predicate
Estimated rows far lower or higher than actual rows

data.title: Takeaway
points: Start with the most expensive operators in the plan
Compare estimated and actual row counts to spot bad estimates
Check for warnings before changing indexes or queries
Read plans from output back to source to understand data flow
data.takeaway: Execution plans are stories. Read them from the final output back to the source to understand why SQL Server chose each step.
